claim: Likeness between cases is relative to a rule or a set of relevant features, not to whole-case resemblance. The court names the rule or ratio and decides which similarities count.
agent_test: On analogy-style tasks, compare plain 'find a similar case' against 'first write the rule the analogue stands for, then re-check it on the target' at equal tokens.

claim: Formal models disagree on what fixes likeness: flat result model (whole case, as strong for same side) vs hierarchical/reason model (stated reasons and factor hierarchy) vs dimensions. The dispute is live and unresolved.
agent_test: Run the same target problems with a flat-overlap selector in code and a hierarchy-aware selector; compare held-out accuracy.

claim: The HYPO/CATO moves (cite the most on-point case, distinguish it, rebut; a factor hierarchy shows a difference is irrelevant) can be coded and checked by a symbolic solver, giving exact ground truth for an analogy step.
agent_test: Implement distinction-checking in code for our analogue mapping, so code, not the model, selects which differences matter (G5).

claim: Reasoning LLMs find factual distinctions between a precedent and a case perfectly (100% on 253 items, 6 models) but fail when relevance must be integrated through a hierarchy (Task 2 64.82-92.09%, Task 3 11.46-33.99%). Figures re-checked against the paper text.
agent_test: Give the agent a surface-overlap check plus a hierarchy-integration check; test whether code-side hierarchy lookup beats model-side integration.

claim: Thinking mode helps hierarchical likeness a lot (Qwen3 78.66% vs 30.04% on Task 2; 33.99% vs 0.00% on Task 3) but more tokens does not mean better: gpt-5 used 4,456 tokens when wrong vs 3,081 when right (+45%).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare one long trace vs several short attempts on distinction tasks; log token count versus correctness.

claim: Models told to abstain when no precedent shares a factor with the case mostly write an argument anyway; abstention ranges 0.00% to 86.67% across eight models (GPT-4o best). Invented factors are rare when an argument is warranted (hallucination accuracy 91-99.6%).
agent_test: Add a code-checked 'no valid analogue' outcome (zero shared relevant features). G6 says never abstain on first pass, so test whether 'no analogue, fall back to plain solve' beats forced mapping.
note: Gap search: the two garbled abstention values (Llama-3-70B 3.33, R1-Distill 23.33) are now read from the HTML table. Prompt stability still untested; one prompt per model, N=30.

claim: Inducing a general rule from 5-10 analogous cases: frontier LLMs over-generalise, explicit rules are recalled far more than implicit ones, CoT trades recall for precision, a verify-each-rule pipeline (SILVER) beats direct/CoT, and a LoRA-tuned 8B model (Mic-F1 73.18) beats prompted frontier models.
agent_test: Test 'induce rule, then verify the rule against every example in code, iterate' against plain CoT rule-writing at equal tokens.

claim: Whether LLMs reason by analogy zero-shot is contested: GPT-3 matched or beat students on digit matrices and letter strings but lost on story analogies (OR 0.37); with permuted alphabets models drop sharply while humans do not; critics say training-data contamination cannot be excluded.
agent_test: Test the agent's analogue mapping on counterfactual (surface-altered) variants, not only the standard form.

claim: Recasting statutory entailment as analogy over (statute, case) pairs left GPT models near chance (49-60%; best retrieval-vote config 57%, not significant); step-by-step prompting often did not help.
agent_test: Check analogue retrieval at equal tokens on problems with exact labels; do not assume prompted analogy beats direct answering.

claim: Retrieval of relevant law by analogy needs more than lexical overlap. Structured reasoning-based query expansion, analogical precedent retrieval, and LLM term generation each beat plain retrievers.
agent_test: Compare surface retrieval of past solved cases against retrieval keyed on the stated rule or structure.

claim: LLMs are weak at the relations between cases: naming the overruled precedent (best 73.31%), verifying a pair (GPT-5 75.42%, Gemini-Pro 42.37% with 131 abstentions), labelling how later courts treated a case (best 79.1% coarse, 67.7% fine; 7 of 15 fine labels F1 0). A reversed-direction control is passed (97-100%), so success is shallow chronology.
agent_test: When using past solved items as memory, verify any claimed relation between items in code rather than trusting the model's assertion.

claim: Accuracy on precedent relations is era-sensitive: older cases much worse than recent (GPT-5 35.29% earliest vs 82.47% modern).
agent_test: Check whether lessons from older problem batches are recalled less reliably than recent ones.
note: Gap search: neither Zhang paper analyses precedent age; claim stays single-source and not tested for lesson memory.

claim: Deep-research agents writing judicial reasoning from precedent give invalid arguments in over 60% of outputs and irrelevant citations in over 53%; removing the key fact lowers quality; arguing the losing side is harder. Law-school IRAC tests show tool spread 73-90%.
agent_test: Do not accept cited-analogue reasoning as evidence; require code-checked applicability.

claim: LLM graders of legal reasoning are uneven: Claude best aligned with experts, some graders near zero or negative correlation on retrieval-augmented outputs.
agent_test: Avoid model graders for analogy quality; use symbolic or held-out checks.

claim: Real judges in a US experiment followed the defendant's sympathy, not a weak precedent: affirmance 87% (13/15) vs 41% (7/17); precedent 64% vs 61%. Chinese judges in a near-replication did move with a strongly favourable precedent (86%/82% vs 40%, N=48).
agent_test: Equal-tokens test that legally irrelevant cues (sympathy, wording) do not change the agent's choice of analogue; vary a legally irrelevant trait.
note: Gap search: GPT-4o follows precedent and ignores sympathy (opposite of judges). Direction found; exact cell counts not read.

claim: Judges used precedent in process (13% vs 4% of time; 68% consulted it before the statute) but only 29% cited it in written reasons: stated reasons do not match used reasons.
agent_test: Compare the agent's stated rationale with which retrieved case actually changed its answer (ablate the case).

claim: Attitudes shift perceived similarity: people call a source case analogous when its outcome fits their policy view, most when cases are moderately similar. Rival account: prior knowledge and framing, not only wanted outcome.
agent_test: Hide the outcome of candidate analogues while selecting them (blind selection) and compare with outcome-visible selection.

claim: Legal expertise in analogy appears to be content knowledge, not a general analogical skill; no data that lawyers or judges are better general analogical reasoners.
agent_test: Domain-specific memory of solved cases should help more than a generic analogy prompt; test per problem class.

claim: Case-based grounding of subjective decisions with retrieved precedents improved human and LLM alignment on moderation/toxicity tasks (humans +16.0 to +23.3 points in 4 of 5 groups).
agent_test: Ground judgement-type tasks in retrieved prior decisions versus written rules at equal tokens.

claim: Structure mapping with schema learning on 100 Illinois tort cases: rule learning from schemas beat analogy and BERT/GPT baselines (47% P@1); pure analogy rose to 72% at P@6.
agent_test: Allow several candidate analogues, then select in code on fresh inputs (S7).

claim: LLMs can induce factor lists from raw opinions; with a human-refined list, factors predict outcomes moderately, and LLM-refined lists were weakest.
agent_test: Have the model propose features but let code or humans fix the feature list; test unrefined versus refined.

claim: Skeptic position: analogy adds nothing beyond rules or principles (Alexander); counter: Sunstein, Schauer.
agent_test: None; theoretical dispute.

claim: LLMs used as judges in the Spamann-Klohn style 2x2 follow precedent and ignore defendant sympathy, unlike real judges and like law students. Newer models do this most (GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Pro 100% law-following vs judges 52%); weaker models do not (Llama 4 Scout and GPT-4.1 50%). Prompts toward legal realism barely moved GPT-4o.
agent_test: Run our scaffold on a weak model with a sympathy cue added to a weak-precedent case; measure whether the cue shifts the answer. Check d01-d03 against the full papers first (press numbers for d02, d03).

claim: Self-generated analogues (model writes relevant examples before solving) give small, consistent gains over 0-shot and few-shot CoT: GSM8K 77.8 vs 76.7, MATH 37.3 vs 34.9, Codeforces Acc@1 15 vs 11, word sorting 75.2 vs 68.4 (GPT-3.5). Diverse exemplars beat non-diverse (77.8 vs 75.9); about 3 exemplars suffice. No token-matched arm and no rule-naming arm.
agent_test: Add a rule-naming arm and a token-matched few-shot arm to the same benchmark.

claim: Out of distribution, transformers match nearest cases rather than apply rules; putting the explicit rule in the input and training the model to recite it step by step lifts accuracy sharply (GPT-3.5 over 95% at 12-digit addition after training on 1-5 digits, over 40 points above scratchpad). Fine-tuned, arithmetic only.
agent_test: Test in prompting only: rule stated in context before the case is applied versus plain nearest-analogue, on perturbed items, at equal tokens.

claim: As of the 2024 evidence, LLM analogy results fall under counterfactual stimuli (digit matrices alt-blank GPT-3.5 0.813 to 0.480, GPT-4 0.810 to 0.477, humans stable at 0.715-0.771). No paper opened here tests reasoning-trained models on the Lewis-Mitchell design, so gap 10 stays open.
agent_test: Always add a counterfactual (relabelled or rule-changed) variant when testing an analogy step.

claim: In legal analogy benchmarks abstention ('unknown') is not scored separately and moves headline accuracy: Gemini-Pro Task 2 42.37% with 131 of 236 unknowns; abstention on no-common-factor cases ranges 0 to 86.67% across models at N=30 with one prompt. No study tests a typed fallback.
agent_test: Give the agent a typed 'no valid analogue, reason X' output and score it apart from errors; run at least three prompt wordings.

claim: Binding precedent and analogy are different constraints: precedent forces a result even when the decider disagrees, analogy is a free choice of the most useful analogue (Schauer).
agent_test: Keep 'follow a binding rule' and 'choose an analogue' as separate operators.
